scenarios.name: Monetary Policy Pivot & Soft Landing
scenarios.description: The Federal Reserve continues a gradual easing cycle to maintain the 4.1% unemployment rate, successfully navigating a soft landing as inflation stabilizes near 3%.

impacts.explanation: Predictable gradual cuts to support moderate GDP growth.
Lower borrowing costs stimulate investment and consumption.

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate for 'oft landings' in modern central banking is relatively high when inflation is cooling without high unemployment; current low unemployment supports this view.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.name: Geopolitical Fragmentation & Supply Chain Shock
scenarios.description: Escalation in regional conflicts (Middle East or Eastern Europe) triggers a secondary energy spike and disrupts critical mineral supply chains.

impacts.explanation: Energy and commodity price shocks increase CPI.
Increased cost of imports and disruption in trade flows.

scenarios.reasoning: Clashing causal forces between geopolitical tension and globalized supply chains; probability adjusted for current high tension levels.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Fiscal Austerity & Debt Servicing Strain
scenarios.description: Rising 10-Year Treasury Yields increase the cost of servicing the $39 trillion national debt, forcing a shift in fiscal priorities and reduced government spending.

impacts.explanation: Interest payments increase the total debt burden rapidly.
Reduced government stimulus and higher private borrowing costs.

scenarios.reasoning: The 1.43% increase in debt is compounding; Treasury yields at 4.69% suggest market concern over fiscal sustainability.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems

scenarios.name: Industrial Re-shoring & Manufacturing Renaissance
scenarios.description: Aggressive domestic industrial policy leads to a surge in capital expenditure for domestic factories, revitalizing industrial production.
scenarios.reasoning: Alignment with long-term deglobalization trends and current industrial production stagnation needing a catalyst.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Stagflationary Persistence
scenarios.description: A 'ticky' inflation environment combined with stagnant GDP growth caused by structural labor shortages and productivity plateaus.

impacts.explanation: Wage-price spirals or structural supply constraints.
Reduced demand leads to higher jobless levels.

scenarios.reasoning: A combination of low GDP growth and stable but non-zero inflation represents a difficult policy regime for the Fed.
tetlockCommandments: Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

methodology: Applied Tetlock's Superforecasting framework. Used base rates for recession/soft-landing probabilities to anchor the 'Outside View'. Subdivided the economy into granular indicators. Combined multiple conflicting causal forces (fiscal vs monetary) to weight scenarios. Calculated forecasts using a weighted average of scenario impacts per indicator to minimize cognitive bias.
geopoliticalSummary: Heightened tensions in multi-theater conflicts create risks of supply chain fracturing and energy price volatility.
geoeconomicSummary: Shift toward domestic manufacturing and protectionist-aligned industrial policy is counterbalancing trade deficit volatility.
currentEventsSummary: The interplay between high debt servicing costs and stabilizing inflation creates a narrow window for a successful monetary pivot.
